quote: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.4 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in October after rising 0.6 percent in September, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.

BLS did not collect survey data for October 2025 because of a lapse in appropriations. For most CPI series, BLS could not publish October 2025 indexes. As a result, BLS cannot publish 12-month percent changes for October 2026 for indexes where October 2025 data are unavailable.

series: CPI-U ex food & energy (seasonally adjusted) MoM
quote: The index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3 percent in October, as it did in September and August.

BLS did not collect survey data for October 2025 because of a lapse in appropriations. For most CPI series, BLS could not publish October 2025 indexes. As a result, BLS cannot publish 12-month percent changes for October 2026 for indexes where October 2025 data are unavailable.
The index for energy increased 0.7 percent in October after rising 5.2 percent in September.
The gasoline index increased 1.0 percent over the month, after advancing 9.1 percent the previous month.
The index for electricity rose 0.9 percent over the month.
The index for food rose 0.5 percent in October after being unchanged in September.
